task.title: Verify and record a CIS deviation
task.shortdesc: Use this task when a CIS-related value is kept, changed, or left for manual verification instead of accepted automatically.

prereq.p: Open a profile that shows a CIS manual-review item, conflict, or intentional deviation from the generated layer.

context.p: Verification means checking the BPM value, schema channel, exported path, and local review evidence. It does not mean BPM has tested Firefox runtime behavior in the target environment.

step.cmd: Open the affected setting and record the recommendation ID, path, current value, source attribution, and schema channel.

info.p: Expected result: the reviewer can identify exactly which BPM-controlled value is under review.

step.cmd: Classify the reason as update governance, proxy routing, evidence retention, unsupported mapping research, deprecated target, or local deployment requirement.

info.p: Expected result: the deviation has a concrete reason instead of a generic exception label.

step.cmd: Validate the profile in BPM and inspect the exported policies.json path that would carry the value.

info.p: Expected result: schema validation and export shape are known before external verification begins.

step.cmd: Perform any runtime, operating-system, network, or audit verification outside BPM using the deployment owner's approved method.

info.p: Expected result: external evidence is collected without claiming that BPM itself proved Firefox behavior.

step.cmd: Record the decision in the external ticket, deployment note, or change-control record, including the BPM profile name, schema channel, recommendation ID, value, reason, owner, and review date.

info.note: BPM does not persist a dedicated CIS exception or waiver object; do not rely on the profile alone as the exception record.

step.cmd: Reopen the profile and confirm the source attribution still shows whether the value is baseline, CIS, manual, imported, converted, or raw.

info.p: Expected result: later reviewers can trace the configured value and find the external record.

result.p: The CIS deviation has actionable verification evidence, an external exception record, and visible BPM source attribution.

example.title: Current 0.9.6 behavior
example.p: Schema, starter preset, and CIS baseline are selected before the saved profile is created. Baseline, CIS, manual, imported, converted, and raw attribution supports review; it does not prove compliance. Certificates and trust have a separate path-level ledger, and manual, imported, converted, raw, unavailable, and blocked states require manual review.

postreq.p: If the reviewer cannot verify the exported path or external evidence, keep the item in manual review and do not describe it as compliant.
